{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjdzc8AAAABZTKmug", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IVzhC6TuU", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IV", "number": 21, "title": "Schedule CD directory reads with real sector progress, resource ownership and cancellation", "body": "## Problem

Related to #17

At `281c404d1725ebae04f5020944a8d5c1c43975b6`, CD commands `0x70` and `0x71` call `load_directory` synchronously and raise EFLS before returning from command execution. That function reads the descriptor sequence and directory sectors through `Media::cooked_sector`, then publishes the complete table. A large directory therefore completes at the same 1075-reference-clock response deadline as a small one.

This path performs strict media validation, but bypasses the runtime decoder's guest-selected correction/retry settings and scheduled sector acquisition. It also creates no in-progress directory operation for AbortFile to cancel and does not acquire the required workspace from the shared sector pool. Existing directory tests primarily inspect results immediately after command response, so they do not establish these hardware effects.

## Expected outcome

Implement one coherent increment: scheduled directory acquisition for ChgDir and ReadDir, integrated with the existing CD drive, decoder, selector resources and completion interrupts.

The primary behavioral reference is the [ST-162-062094 CD Communication Interface manual](https://antime.kapsi.fi/sega/files/ST-162-062094.pdf), §§3.1–3.2/table 3.2, §§6.2.1–6.2.3/table 6.1, and §8.2.8 functions 8.1–8.6. Directory acquisition must have an observable lifetime beyond command response. Workspace requires an empty sector. AbortFile pauses access, preserves partition data and selector settings, and invalidates a table interrupted during directory acquisition. Other drive commands remain executable during filesystem work.

Keep physical seek latency assumptions explicit. Reuse the deterministic drive model; this task does not require measured console timings.

## Context and reproduction

Relevant implementation:

- `src/cd.rs:1427–1468`: synchronous ChgDir/ReadDir and immediate EFLS.
- `src/cd.rs:1564–1669`: descriptor/directory extraction and table publication.
- `src/cd.rs:475–632`: existing scheduled drive reads, correction settings and retries.
- `src/media.rs:423–438,477–492`: runtime decoding versus strict cooked-sector extraction.
- `src/cd.rs:1541–1546`: AbortFile currently cancels only file payload reads.

Reproduce the timing gap with an original multi-sector directory: clear EFLS, issue ChgDir, advance through command response, and inspect EFLS and scope. Current code has already published the complete table without advancing through its media sectors. Fill other partitions while leaving the work partition empty to expose the missing workspace accounting.

Scope includes directory acquisition, its necessary scheduling/resource state, completion/error handling and cancellation. Preserve ReadFile, existing directory formats/windows, boot parsing and unrelated device behavior. Do not expand into new media formats or the complete BIOS CD-library ABI.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Implement resumable ChgDir/ReadDir work. Native vectors distinguish command response from filesystem completion and prove descriptor/directory acquisition progresses through scheduled sector deadlines. Publishing a table after an arbitrary delay while extracting it synchronously is insufficient.
- [ ] Route acquired sectors through runtime correction/retry handling. Test clean, correctable and uncorrectable original raw sectors, disabled correction, finite retries and cancellation during infinite retry. Check command responses, drive status, table availability and completion flags separately; never overwrite a retained command response to fabricate an asynchronous result.
- [ ] Account for directory workspace in the shared 200-sector pool. Exercise full capacity and a single remaining free sector alongside host reservations. Assert bounded behavior, no over-allocation, preservation of unrelated sectors and release of temporary ownership on completion/cancellation.
- [ ] Add cancellation vectors before the first read, between directory sectors and immediately before completion. Cover AbortFile, tray open, software reset, CD disable and media replacement. Check table invalidation where specified, resource release and absence of later stale publication or IRQ. Distinguish invalid command parameters from errors discovered during media acquisition.
- [ ] Verify concurrent status/drive commands and independent host/selector transfers during directory work. Use literal event traces and unchanged payload canaries. Include SCU delivery of the masked/unmasked EFLS interrupt and guest acknowledgement, rather than testing HIRQ readback alone.
- [ ] Native tests cover root/child navigation, ReadDir windows, multi-sector directories, existing malformed-record/extent cases and 1×/2× operation. Compare results and event ordering across advancement chunks of 1, 3, 17 and 10000 clocks. Derive expectations independently of implementation helpers and document unspecified timing choices.
- [ ] Add an original MIT-licensed SH-2 diagnostic and reproducible media builder. The guest issues commands, measures progress with FRT, handles completion and records directory-derived results. Run identical media through native Machine and rebuilt production Wasm in the headless browser. Include changed directory operands, omitted-command and mid-operation abort controls, repeated cold boots, and a negative control demonstrating that the inherited synchronous implementation fails a substantive assertion. Host code may supply media and inspect results only.
- [ ] Preserve the existing directory/raw-media/decode corpus and all demonstrations, including Star Collector completion/restart, Prism Courier and Hardware Lab. Adapt timing-dependent waits or response expectations only with a documented specification rationale; retain substantive bounds, malformed-media, payload, audio, input, backup and privacy assertions.
- [ ] Update the conformance matrix and validation record with implementation/test/spec links, actual results and remaining deviations. Pass `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo build --locked`, `cargo test --locked`, native all-target and Wasm Clippy with warnings denied, `sh scripts/build-web.sh`, all fixture/media reproduction checks, and the complete `npm run test:browser` suite under `/saturn-rust/` without required skips.

This increment leaves the remaining #17 CPU/peripheral, multiprocessor/bus/reset, SCU/DSP, video/audio, CD/media/HLE, SMPC and comprehensive integration requirements outstanding. Neither this Issue nor green CI establishes umbrella completion or broad commercial-game compatibility; commercial compatibility remains unverified.

## Optional validation

None required. Original fixtures and autonomous native/Wasm/browser checks provide the acceptance evidence; personal firmware, commercial discs and physical hardware are unnecessary.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
